title: India unveils first AI-driven fighter drone FWD Supreme for long-range strikes and fighter escort
key_facts: On 13 Oct 2026 Bengaluru-based Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace unveiled a full-scale static prototype of the FWD Supreme in New Delhi.
The company describes it as India's first indigenous AI-driven autonomous combat drone, a design objective not a flown aircraft.
Targets include a range above 1,500 km, a payload of 350 kg and a top speed of Mach 0.85.
The company's concept would assign 15 to 20 AI-piloted 'loyal wingmen' to one crewed fighter, at $3 to 5 million each.
India's Ministry of Defence acquisition chief A. Anbarasu attended, but no government contract or funding has been confirmed.
The smaller Supreme Lite has completed taxi trials but not flown; its first flight missed a Q3 2026 target and is now expected in six to eight weeks.

why_it_matters_hint: An Indian start-up shows a mock-up of a cheap AI-piloted combat drone, but nothing has flown and no government order exists.
notes: Headline says 'unveils' an AI-driven fighter drone, but the article says it is a static prototype with unflown demonstrators.
